paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Solomon has a huge plan, and he doesn't rush at it alone. He asks Hiram for cedars, a skilled craftsman and a crew, and he promises real wages for the work (2 Chronicles 2:3, 7, 10). Big work for God gets done with other people, and that includes help from folks outside Israel.

Then listen to what Solomon says about himself. He says the house will be great, "for our God is greater than all gods." And then he asks, "But who is able to build a house for Him, since the heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain Him?" (2 Chronicles 2:5-6). Over 150,000 workers, and he's STILL humble enough to say God is bigger than anything he could build. I spent years in a drawer, and I know a little about being small. Being small in front of God is exactly the right size, and that's where good work begins.

So here's your takeaway, baker. Give God your very best, and keep His greatness bigger than your plans. Hiram does it too. Before he says a word about logs, he says, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth!" (2 Chronicles 2:12). Start with God, work with the people He puts beside you, and don't get too big for your apron. The building is only getting started, so don't leave!
